title: feat: approve agent sign-ins with T3 Connect instead of a code
author: juliusmarminge
head: 8a6dc9f9d5407f5cc7d1ae3f67ecbeff82f3dade
body:
Signing an outside agent (Cursor, Claude Code, ChatGPT) into an environment reached over T3 Connect meant pasting a sign-in code, even though the owner is already signed in to T3 Connect.

## What changes

On the environment's T3 Connect (tunnel) address, the agent sign-in page now offers **Approve <level> with T3 Connect**:

1. The page stores a random nonce, the chosen level and the request in this tab's `sessionStorage`, then opens `/approve-agent`.
2. app.t3.codes signs in with Clerk and authorizes against that environment through the relay. The relay only does this for the environment's linked owner.
3. It mints a one-use app approval code at that level, but only if the sign-in page's origin is that environment's relay address. The code goes back to the page in the URL fragment.
4. The page uses the code only when the nonce, level and request match what this tab stored. Anything else is discarded, never filled in. The fragment is stripped right away.

There are no relay changes and no new proof type. This reuses the existing Connect credentials, which already carry `access:write`, and the existing app approval codes. The server sends `connectSignIn: { environmentId, hostedAppUrl }` only when the environment is linked and the request is on its tunnel hostname. `hostedAppUrl` comes from `T3CODE_HOSTED_APP_URL`, so nightly installs can point at nightly.app.t3.codes. The paste-a-code and browser-session paths are unchanged.

## Security review

body:

The wait was a deliberate 500 ms timer from [#7817](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/7817). It gave a double-click time to start a rename before the native menu opened. This removes the timer, so one click opens the menu at once on every surface.

title: fix(mobile): Android PDF preview double-tap zoom and easier link taps
author: juliusmarminge
head: ba783be9aa3382d6540865eff61b3b40b94c902c
body:
## Problem

On Android, the PDF preview (`react-native-pdf-jsi` 6.1.0) ignored double-tap: the page never zoomed. Citation links such as `[13]` were also hard to hit, while long URL links worked every time.

## Cause

**Double-tap (library bug, not our hosting).** Android's `GestureDetector` delivers `onDoubleTap` and then `onDown` for the same second-tap `ACTION_DOWN`. The viewer's `onDown` called `stopMotion()`, which cancelled the zoom `ValueAnimator` that `onDoubleTap` had started a moment earlier. The zoom was undone within the same event, so it never showed. Pinch was not affected (separate `ScaleGestureDetector`).

The bug is in the viewer, not in where we host it. The PDF a chat `.pdf` link opens sits in an RN `Modal` (`FilePreviewModal.android.tsx`). After the patch, double-tap works there and in the Files route (`WorkspaceFileWebPreview`) without any app-side change.

**Link taps.** `handleTap` only matched a touch inside the link rect. In this paper the citation rects cover only the digits (e.g. `13` in `[13]`, 7–12pt wide and about 9pt tall), so a fingertip on the bracket or slightly below missed.

## Change

New pnpm patch `patches/react-native-pdf-jsi@6.1.0.patch` (one file, `PdfViewerView.kt`):

- Stop motion in `onTouchEvent` on `ACTION_DOWN`, before the gesture detectors run. `onDown` now only returns `true`.
- Hit-test links with 10dp of slop in screen space, converted to page points at the current zoom, and pick the nearest link when several qualify.

title: ci(mobile): build Android store releases on Blacksmith
author: juliusmarminge
head: a304b46db5a696426c7428d42359f79fa7399aba
body:
## Problem

Android store builds (EAS profile `production`, submitted to the Play internal track) run on EAS cloud builders and take about 42 minutes. Gradle accounts for 39 minutes of that on 4 vCPU with no cache, compiling native code for four ABIs and running release lint.

## Change

**Android** builds in a new `android` job in `mobile-eas-production.yml` on `blacksmith-32vcpu-ubuntu-2404`. The job runs `eas build --local` and then `eas submit --platform android --profile production --path ` to the existing internal track.

- **ARM only.** The `production` profile sets `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures=armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a`. Development, preview, and emulator profiles keep all four ABIs. In the check runs, CMake built only `arm64-v8a` and `armeabi-v7a`, and the AAB contained only `base/lib/arm64-v8a` and `base/lib/armeabi-v7a`. The job now fails if any other ABI shows up.
- **No release lint.** The profile's `gradleCommand` is `:app:bundleRelease -x lintVitalAnalyzeRelease -x lintVitalRelease`. No `lintVital*` task ran in the check runs. Lint still runs in CI elsewhere.
- **Caches on one Blacksmith sticky disk:**
  - Gradle user home, with `org.gradle.caching=true` and no daemon.
  - ccache, wired in through `CMAKE_{C,CXX}_COMPILER_LAUNCHER`, which AGP passes through to CMake.
  - The pnpm store.
  - The EAS working directory, set to a fixed `EAS_LOCAL_BUILD_WORKINGDIR`. The fixed path keeps ccache keys stable, and putting it on the same disk as the store lets [...]

title: fix(mobile): the composer and search bars move with their iOS columns
author: juliusmarminge
head: c7b56db893d907c067ec14b253c7fc68f1211965
body:
Two iOS workspace motion fixes for the bars beside a thread.

### The composer resizes with the feed

Toggling the sidebar beside a thread made the composer shift on its own. The composer follows the native column directly. Since https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33459 the feed waits for the render that hands it its new width, so the two changed size 2–3 frames apart.

On the native columns, `ThreadDetailScreen` now measures its own width and gives the feed (through `WorkspaceSettledContentWidthContext`, which `ThreadFeed` already reads) and the composer that width in one render. Both keep their old width while UIKit slides the column, then resize in the same frame.

One trade-off: while it holds its old width, the composer moves with the column. When the sidebar opens, its right end passes under the right-hand rail for about two frames, where before the feed's text did. When the sidebar closes, the composer's left end still slides under the outgoing sidebar's search pill for a frame or two; that's UIKit's animation and happens on `main` too.

#### Evidence

iPhone Duo simulator, unfolded landscape, a long thread at its end. Consecutive 30 fps frames of the bottom of the screen; before is `main`, after is this branch, same native client.

title: fix(web): checking for updates finds provider updates on every machine
author: t3dotgg
head: 73eed4c17da74af730b16e6dde6163f99e2c54ee
body:
Each server caches the latest provider version for one hour. After a new Claude Code release, only some machines showed the update. "Check for updates" did not help, because it only checked the T3 Code app.

Now a check for updates also tells every connected machine to drop that cache and look again. The update dialog does the same when it opens, so machines that were behind add their rows while you read it.

## Changes

- The sidebar update button and Settings > About "Check for updates" also check provider versions on every connected machine you can manage. The button stays busy until all machines answer. A failed machine gets one toast line.
- When one update is already known, the sidebar button opens the update dialog and does not check. The dialog now starts the same check on open and shows "Checking for more…" until it ends. This check shows no toast on failure, because the user did not ask for it.
- No server or contract change. It uses the existing `server.refreshProviders` call with `refreshModels: true`, so older servers work too.

title: fix(web): clicked workspace areas no longer show the focus ring after a stray key
author: t3dotgg
head: 2c706af82964983a61defe1dbbce66499524b70e
body:
## Problem

Click an empty part of the conversation or home area. Then press any bare key, such as Shift or Meta. A 2px focus ring appears around the whole area. A window switch can send that key for you (Hyprland focus-follows-mouse, a Super-key window switch), so the ring shows up with no keyboard navigation at all.

The cause is `[data-workspace-area]:focus-visible`. Chromium turns `:focus-visible` on for the element that already has focus when a key arrives. The same selector made the window-return check treat a clicked area as "reached from the keyboard", so the caret did not go back to the composer.

## Change

The workspace focus controller now marks an area with `data-workspace-keyboard-focus` only when keyboard focus arrives on it: F6, a focus request, or focus that returns from a dialog. A pointer press, focus moving elsewhere, and dispose clear the mark. Window activation refocuses the same element, so it does not count as an arrival.

The ring in `index.css` and `shouldRefocusComposerOnWindowFocus` read the mark instead of `:focus-visible`.

This replaces [#28191](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/28191) by @juliusmarminge, which was 1160 commits behind `main` and had a conflict. The five original commits are kept with their authorship. The one conflict was in `ChatView.logic.ts`: `main` renamed the sidebar selector to `[data-sidebar-row]:focus-visible`, and this branch keeps that name.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#28166

body:

Cmd+W did not close Developer Tools when they had focus. The shortcut should close DevTools while retaining its existing renderer behavior for closing tabs and terminals.

Add a hidden native menu item that closes the focused DevTools instance. Let Cmd+W reach the renderer in the app window, and keep repeated presses from closing multiple tabs or terminals.

title: fix(models): new models also surface the CLI update that supports them
author: t3dotgg
head: b40bfc3f512fabee26b3258445c9129c4a0b0572
body:
When a new model drops, the matching Claude Code release usually ships the same day. T3 caches each provider's latest CLI version for an hour, so a new model could appear in the picker while the update prompt for the CLI that runs it stayed hidden for up to an hour. Today Fable 5.2 showed up, but Claude Code 2.1.321 did not appear in the update dialog. On 2.1.319, Fable 5.2 runs with a 200k window and compacts early.

Now, when the model picker's check ([#33511](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/33511)) finds a changed manifest, the server clears the latest-version cache before it probes providers. New models and the CLI update that supports them show up together. A picker open with no manifest change costs nothing extra.

title: feat(models): the model picker checks for new models when it opens
author: t3dotgg
head: 704656710c8e821f16369282cc9b98c0efbe9baa
body:
## Problem

The server refetches the model manifest at most once an hour. When a new model ships, a user can wait up to an hour to see it, unless they know about **Settings → Providers → Refresh provider status**.

## Fix

Opening a model picker now asks the server to check for new models.

- **Server:** `ModelManifest.refreshOnDemand` refetches a manifest that is older than 5 minutes (GitHub's raw CDN caches about that long). `ProviderRegistry.refreshModelCatalog` probes the providers only when the manifest `updatedAt` differs from the one the last successful full probe pass started with. If nothing changed, the request costs one cache check.
- **Wire:** `server.refreshProviders` has a new optional field, `modelCatalogOnly`. A new `modelCatalogRefresh` capability keeps new clients from sending it to an old server, which would ignore the field and probe every provider.
- **Web and desktop:** `ProviderModelPicker` sends the request each time it opens. This covers the composer and all Settings pickers.
- **Mobile:** the thread settings sheet sends the request when the model list mounts.

The result comes back on the config stream, so an open picker updates in place. The hourly background refresh and the manual refresh button do not change. The request is skipped when provider update checks are off.

## Verification

- `ModelManifest.test.ts`: an on-demand refresh refetches after 5 minutes; a routine refresh does not.
- `ProviderRegistry.test.ts`: providers are probed once when  [...]

threads.body:
🟠 **High** `provider/ProviderRegistry.ts:1082`

When `refreshAll()` fails, `probedManifestUpdatedAt` still advances to the new `updatedAt`, so later picker openings skip probing that manifest and newly published models remain missing. Because `recoverRefreshFailure` preserves the cached snapshots, record the timestamp only after `refreshAll()` completes successfully and leave it unchanged on failure.

title: fix(mobile): the unfolded Duo sidebar no longer pops back in while resizing Files

On the unfolded Duo, dragging the Files inspector divider could pop the sidebar back in partway through the drag, squeezing the thread between the sidebar and the inspector.

The native workspace steps the sidebar aside when the inspector leaves the page too narrow. title: chore(mobile): update react-native-pdf-jsi to 6.1.0 and link it on Android only
author: juliusmarminge
head: 1059e25ca667c1b1feff1b4f882b39a3e269ffd7
body:
We were on `react-native-pdf-jsi` 5.0.0 with a local patch. Only Android uses it: iOS previews PDFs in a WebView (`PdfPreview.tsx`), which WebKit renders natively. This updates to **6.1.0**, links the library on Android only, and drops both its patch and its config plugin.

## Why 6.1.0 and not 6.1.1

6.1.1 can't build on Android. It stopped shipping PDFium in the npm package, and its `downloadPdfium` Gradle task fetches `pdfium-android-r1.zip` from the upstream GitHub release `pdfium-android-r1`. That release was never published: the URL returns 404, and the only 6.x release is `v6.1.0`. 6.1.0 still bundles PDFium, so it builds offline. Once upstream publishes the asset, moving to 6.1.1+ is a version bump.

## Changes

- `react-native-pdf-jsi` 5.0.0 → 6.1.0 in `apps/mobile/package.json` and the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog.
- **Android only.** `expo.autolinking.ios.exclude` keeps it out of the iOS build, so iOS no longer compiles a PDF engine it never runs. `expo-modules-autolinking react-native-config` lists it for Android and not for iOS, and the iOS build log has no trace of its pod.
- **Config plugin removed.** On Android it only forced New Architecture on (already on) and wrote `pdfJsiEnableOcr=false` (the Gradle default when the property is unset). title: fix(client): finishing a long background thread no longer freezes the app
author: juliusmarminge
head: 0b7b29951f2985f5b90c93de53e9740caaa039ce
body:
## Problem

A desktop performance trace showed two main-thread freezes of 1.7s and 1.6s while the user was typing in the composer. The keystrokes queued up and replayed afterwards (16 at once after the first freeze).

Both freezes had the same cause. A thread that had been running in the background finished. `runningThreadKeepAliveAtom` stopped mounting its live state, the registry removed the atom on the next `setTimeout(0)`, and the thread-state scope finalizer saved the **entire live projection** to the thread cache in one task:

| Step | Cost per freeze |
|---|---|
| Schema encode (`Schema.fromJsonString(StoredOrchestrationThreadSnapshot)`) | ~0.35–0.7s |
| JSON stringify | ~0.3–0.7s |
| `IDBObjectStore.put` copying the string | ~0.5–0.6s |

`KeyboardChatScrollView` stops all keyboard writes while frozen. `useKeyboardScrollToEnd` freezes it while it scrolls the thread to the end. title: fix(mobile): a full swipe on a thread row finishes even if the pan is cancelled
author: juliusmarminge
head: 223d4d5bd80139fe66133171404b6b34f3f9d696
body:
## Problem

If a thread row's dismissal starts while its pan is still active (for example, the thread gets archived while a finger is on the row), the row disables its swipeable, which cancels the pan. RNGH's canceled-pan path in `ReanimatedSwipeable` then started the return spring on the same shared value. That replaced the dismissal animation, so the dismissal's completion callback never ran and the archive/delete waiting on it never finished. CodeRabbit flagged this. It has not been reproduced on a device.

## Change

- `patches/react-native-gesture-handler@3.5.0.patch`: before the canceled-pan path starts its spring, it now calls `onSwipeableRelease`. The hook gets a new `canceled` argument (`false` on a normal release), and returning true still means the caller owns translation. Both `src/` and `lib/module` are patched, plus the typings.
- `thread-swipe-actions.tsx`: `handleRelease` keeps ownership while the row is dismissing, as it already did on a normal release. It never commits a full swipe from a canceled pan, so an ordinary canceled pan still springs back to rest.

Android uses the same JS `ReanimatedSwipeable` path, so this one change covers it.

Known gap, not addressed here: pan *updates* that arrive between the start of the dismissal and the cancel also write `appliedTranslation`. Those can still interrupt the timing. That only happens if the finger moves during the frame or two before `enabled={false}` lands.

author: juliusmarminge
head: e6759696ac68e03d6bbadc5ac14f9863edb3e9b3
body:
Every nightly since 10:15 UTC on 2026-11-09 fails at "Build CLI single-executable" on five of six desktop targets:

```
ServerCliExecutableImportError: binMain.mjs imports file-backed packages that a single-executable cannot resolve: undici
```

https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/33093 gave the Cursor Origin client platform-node's undici client for HTTP/2. Swapping only the `Agent` import is not enough, because `makeUndici` itself pulls the module in.

The Origin client now uses platform-node's `node:http` client with a keep-alive agent, as `GitHubHttpClient` already does. Connections still stay open between requests, but Origin loses HTTP/2, so a pull request's parallel reads use separate connections.

- I built the executable's CLI bundle (`T3CODE_PACK_EXE=bundle vp pack`) before and after. Before: `binMain.mjs` line 29 is `import Undici, * as import_undici from "undici";`. After: no `undici` import remains.

title: fix(mobile): the thread feed re-wraps once when an iOS column resizes
author: juliusmarminge
head: 7e05f2887c6839d740f08911c9ced37930a30261
body:
On iOS, opening, closing or dragging the Files inspector next to a thread changes the thread column's width. On a long thread the feed visibly broke: rows overlapped for several frames, then the feed jumped once or twice before landing at its end.

Two causes:

1. **Rows re-wrapped before the list knew.** The native column resize re-lays the feed's text at the new width immediately, but Legend List positions rows absolutely and only hears their new heights through `onLayout`. For ~4 frames, taller or shorter rows sat at their old offsets. In a split, `ThreadFeed` now pins the list to the width JS measured. Rows re-wrap in the render that hands the list its new width (`extraData.viewportWidth`), and Legend List measures them in that same commit.
2. **The end landed a frame late.** Even with a single re-wrap, Legend List's native MVCP kept the top visible row in place, and end following scrolled back to the end a frame later. The Legend List patch holds the end in the same pass while the feed is following it. https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/28125 dropped our older `sizeChangeAnchor` patch, which had covered this. It's small enough for Jay to upstream.

Neither change is enough on its own. With only the pinned width, the feed re-wraps once and then jumps about 35 pt a couple of frames later.

### Evidence

iPhone Duo simulator, unfolded landscape, a long thread at its end, the stock `main` native client. Before is `main`; after is this branch. Each strip is consecutive 3 [...]

title: perf(mobile): threads open over the socket without an extra HTTP round trip
author: t3dotgg
head: 04e7a4c685e6287f46ada5598787f7ec653a8b02
body:
## Problem

On bad wifi, opening a thread on mobile waits for an HTTP snapshot round trip before the socket even subscribes. The same bounded window already comes over the socket. Reconnects also read the environment descriptor twice in a row.

## Change

- **Thread open skips HTTP.** When the server pages snapshots, a cold open uses the socket snapshot. It tries this one time. After any failure, defect, or dropped session, the next cold attempt asks HTTP, so a missing thread still shows as deleted and a bad socket snapshot still shows the thread. Authorization errors show at once, because those are never retried.
- **Connect reuses the descriptor a check just read.** A route or host check gives its descriptor to the next authorization of that URL, one time. It is reused only over HTTPS, only when the environment id matches, and only within 5 s. A plain LAN address can belong to another machine after a network change, so it keeps its fresh identity check before any token is sent. A failed check clears the entry.
- **Per-frame socket deflate is dropped.** #33172 also deflated frames by hand for iOS and added `fflate`. But the iOS socket from [#32288](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/32288) already negotiates permessage-deflate, so that path never ran. I reverted it.

## Scope and approval

title: fix(server): background command results reach a running Codex goal
author: t3dotgg
head: cfcc50334d0961436b24928ebb139bbbbfaeeaf6
body:
A Codex `/goal` keeps one T3 run open until the goal ends, because each continuation turn joins the same run. Background command results are sent as queued notices, and queued notices only start when the run ends. So during a goal, the agent did not learn that its background commands had finished. On Theo's fleet since Nov 4, 10 of these notices waited over 10 minutes in goal threads, and one waited 49 hours.

While the goal is active, a background command notice that carries its own text now steers into the running turn. This is the same path [#29909](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/29909) added for delegated task questions, with the same steering-capability and Stop checks. Outside a goal, these notices still queue as before.

Proof: a new row in the `SteeringCompletion` integration test sends a background command notice during a run with an active goal. On `main` the notice queues and nothing steers. With this change it steers into the running turn with its full text. A second row shows the notice still queues when no goal is active. `vp run check:changed` passes. The 49-hour wait comes from a read-only query of zbook's state database. I did not run a real-provider end-to-end test.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 pass with GPT-6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved

title: fix(server): Codex /goal no longer tries to create the goal twice
author: t3dotgg
head: 8a8525bf4e45705e90075b2980527695a1ebbade
body:
Codex `/goal` in T3 tripped over its own tools. T3 sets the goal, then starts the first goal turn with the user message `Start working toward this goal: X`. The model read that as a request to make a goal, called `create_goal`, and Codex rejected it with "cannot create a new goal because this thread has an unfinished goal". It usually rewrote the objective in that call too. This happened in the first turn of every Codex goal thread I checked across 4 machines. The Codex CLI does not hit this, because it starts the first goal turn with its own goal prompt.

The first goal turn now says the goal is already set and not to call `create_goal`.

Proof: I replayed T3's exact sequence (goal set paused, `turn/start` with the text, goal set active) against a real `codex app-server` 0.167.0. With the old text, 5 of 5 runs called `create_goal` and got rejected. With the new text, 0 of 5 did. All 10 runs finished the task.

title: ci(release): retry transient GitHub API errors when resolving the release commit
author: t3dotgg
head: 5f73b341ce6869e2a681672113304a5627105588
body:
## Problem

The nightly Release workflow failed twice this week in its first job, "Resolve release commit". The cause was GitHub API errors, not our code. Run [41285726049](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/41285726049) got `HttpError: terminated` and run [42057337624](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42057337624) got a `504`. `actions/github-script` does not retry by default.

## Change

This sets the action's built-in `retries: 3` on that step. Octokit's retry plugin retries 5xx errors and dropped connections. Octokit reports a dropped connection as status 500. It retries only the failed request, after waits of 1, 4, and 9 seconds. It does not run the script or its release assertions again, and it still does not retry 400/401/403/404/422.

## Scope and approval

This is a maintainer change found in the daily CI flake pass. It adds 2 lines to one step and makes no product change. All 4 API calls in that step (`compareCommitsWithBasehead` twice, `listReleases`, `getCommit`) are reads, so a retry cannot repeat a write.

## Verification

- actionlint shows no new findings on `release.yml`.
- I read `.github/scripts/check-nightly-release.cjs` and the github-script v8 bundle to confirm that the calls are reads and that the retry applies to these errors.
- Not checked: PR CI cannot run the scheduled release path. The first real run is the next nightly after merge.

author: t3dotgg
head: 8ea4c3b722708a4f149d74e342237bcb9fb79026
body:
## Problem

Azure Trusted Signing sometimes answers with `InternalError - An internal error has occurred.`. On Nov 3, three scheduled releases in one hour failed on both Windows legs. The error came on the certificate-chain call ([job log](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/41676634775/job/126060242207)) and on the sign call. One failed jsign call fails the whole electron-builder packaging step. electron-builder's own sign retry only matches host-name and file-lock messages, so it does not help here.

## Change

`scripts/lib/windows-jsign.ts` retries the single jsign call. It does not retry the packaging step.

- jsign stderr still goes to the log as before. The script also keeps the last 64 KiB of stderr to classify the failure. No new output is printed except a one-line retry warning with the file path and attempt number.
- Only recognized transient errors get a retry: Azure `InternalError - `, `HTTP Error 429/5xx`, `SocketTimeoutException`, `ConnectException`, and `Connection reset`. There are at most 3 retries, with a 5 s / 10 s / 20 s backoff. Bad credentials (for example `AADSTS…`), permission errors, unsupported input, and other failures still fail on the first attempt.
- Each attempt signs a fresh copy in a hidden temp directory next to the file. The copy replaces the file by rename only when jsign exits 0. A failed or partly written attempt never changes the input, and each retry starts from the original bytes. The temp directory is removed in both case [...]

title: fix(antigravity): agy CLI threads open in Full access and Auto-accept edits
author: t3dotgg
head: 64b56d63f84d37b641f66f6d8413d170914e2283
body:
Using the Antigravity `agy` CLI as the custom binary broke most threads. T3 sent the managed runtime's `yolo` (Full access) and `auto_edit` (Auto-accept edits) session modes. The CLI only knows `default`, `accept-edits`, and `plan`, so the session failed to open:

```text
Invalid value "yolo" for session config option "mode": expected one of default, accept-edits, plan
```

Full access is the default mode, so every new CLI thread failed. See [#32856](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/32856).

## Fix

When the runtime is the CLI, T3 sends `default` in place of `yolo` and `auto_edit`. In `default` the CLI asks before it acts, and T3 already answers those requests from the live permission setting: Full access allows, Auto-accept edits allows edits, and Supervised asks. So permission changes apply on the next turn, with no bypass flag and no process restart. The managed runtime is unchanged.

This takes over [#32875](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/32875) by @Q3yp, and their commits are kept. That PR launched `agy acp --dangerously-skip-permissions` for Full access and replaced the session on every permission change. Review found that a downgrade made while a session was still opening could leave the bypass flag on. Answering permissions in T3 removes the flag, and with it the race, and cuts the change to about 13 source lines.

## Problem

Every Linux release build downloads the AppImage runtime, FPM (for the deb target), and the 7-Zip that unpacks FPM from GitHub releases. The last seven successful Linux x64 builds downloaded all three. On Nov 8 a nightly Linux x64 build failed with `Response code 504 (Gateway Timeout)` right after these downloads ([job log](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42476781466/job/128720096784)). One `actions/cache` step on the Linux legs of `release-desktop.yml` keeps only the three raw archives, about 23 MB, at electron-builder's default cache path:

- `~/.cache/electron-builder/fpm@*/fpm-*.7z`
- `~/.cache/electron-builder/7zip@*/7zip-linux-*.tar.gz`

The cache is safe because of how app-builder-lib 26.16.1 uses these archives. Before it extracts an archive found at `//`, it hashes it against the SHA-256 pinned in `toolsets/linux.js` (AppImage and FPM) and `toolsets/7zip.js`. The key is the arch plus a hash of those two toolset files. It changes only when app-builder-lib changes a pinned tool, not on unrelated lockfile changes. A miss, or an older source ref that uses other tool paths, falls back to the download we do today.

title: fix(desktop): update xa11y to 0.15.4 so App Shots read window text faster
author: MatthewFeroz
head: d210e11ac11e260506867b67fc27d251be6b56d6
body:
On Windows, App Shots of big pages lose their window text. xa11y 0.13 asks the browser about one element at a time, and a large page takes longer than the 3-second accessibility limit, so the shot gets only the window title. xa11y 0.15 reads each element with fewer cross-process calls ([xa11y#450](https://github.com/xa11y/xa11y/pull/450)). This PR updates to 0.15.4. On the page below, a direct read of the window drops from 1.9 s to 0.85 s.

0.15 also changes two things App Shots relied on. With only the version bump, every Windows shot arrived with no text at all:

- `App.foreground` now returns the whole process, with its windows as children ([xa11y#436](https://github.com/xa11y/xa11y/pull/436)). App Shots treated that result as the window, so it never matched. It now looks through the foreground process's windows.
- On Windows, bounds, screenshot regions and element positions are now physical desktop pixels instead of DIPs ([xa11y#439](https://github.com/xa11y/xa11y/pull/439)).
  - Window bounds already come from `GetWindowRect` in physical pixels, so the capture region and window matching now use them as-is. Only the flash overlay, an Electron window, still converts to DIPs.
  - The focus helper converts T3's own window bounds with `screen.dipToScreenRect` before matching.
  - The helper's `App.list()` fallback is gone. In 0.15, `App.byPid(...).children()` already returns T3's window, while 0.13 returned two unnamed groups there.

The update also lowers the Linux [...]

title: fix(mobile): Android chip taps open the chip from either half
author: maria-rcks
head: 88191209924f5589ed13b8516b2fb83dde76a86c
body:
On Android, tapping the right half of a composer chip (file, skill, or context) moved the cursor instead of opening the chip. A chip is one replacement span, so a tap past its middle reports the chip's end offset, which the hit test excluded.

A tap now opens a chip when its offset is anywhere from the chip's start to its end and the touch lands inside the chip's drawn bounds on its line. That also stops a tap in the blank space below a chip that ends the draft from opening it. iOS is unaffected. This changes the Android native fingerprint, so merge timing should follow a matching store build.

Scope: maintainer fix of an obvious bug, split out of #31207 (where ScriptedAlchemy found it) so that PR stays JS-only.

- CI, including Mobile Native Static Analysis (ktlint, detekt).
- The fix build compiles and installs on an Android 16 emulator dev client (fingerprint 34bfa078 for an earlier head of this branch).
- Two independent code reviews of the hit test, repeated on this head: adjacent chips, soft wraps, chips before a newline, scroll and padding, left-half taps, long press, stale tokens after an edit.
- Not yet verified on a device: the before/after taps themselves. Both shared emulators were held by other sessions; a recording will be added here.

**Check the chip’s vertical bounds before accepting its end offset.**

If a chip ends the draft, a tap below its line can still resolve to `token.end`: Android clamps the touch to the last text line. When the tap’s x-coordinate falls within the chip, `chipContainsX` then fires `onComposerContextPress` outside the drawn chip. Pass the touch y-coordinate to this helper and require the touch to be on the chip’s drawn line. ([android.googlesource.com](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/%2B/64eaba03c5db8b431aef8a88d40593631951fe99/core/java/android/widget/TextView.java))

After a trailing chip is deleted, a tap at its former start can crash the touch handler with `IndexOutOfBoundsException` on Android 16: `chipContains` calls `getPrimaryHorizontal(token.end)` using stale token bounds before the later text/source check runs. Validate the token’s bounds and source against `editor.text` before calling `chipContains`.

```suggestion

                  it.end  it.start &&

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Reject stale token offsets before measuring chip bounds.**

If a native edit shortens the draft before `tokens` updates, a tap can match a token whose `end` exceeds `editor.length()`. `chipContains` then passes that invalid offset to `layout.getPrimaryHorizontal(token.end)`. Android defines text-line measurements for offsets within the line, so this can crash before the existing length check runs. Move the token-range check ahead of `chipContains`, including a non-negative `start`. ([android.googlesource.com](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/%2B/refs/heads/android17-release/core/java/android/text/Layout.java))

@​maria-rcks Confirmed: `8819120992` checks `end` against the editor length before calling `chipContains`.

The current JavaScript token producers derive starts from match indices. I agree that a separate `start >= 0` check is not needed for this path.

Users assume the Source control writing style setting only shapes commit messages, so they never find out that Custom instructions also controls generated pull request titles and descriptions. The section was called "Writing & review", the row "Source control writing style", and its copy talked about "change descriptions" and "change requests".

The section is now "Commits & pull requests" and the row is "Commit and pull request writing". Each style's description names commit messages and pull request titles and descriptions, and the custom instructions placeholder shows a pull request example. "Follow change request templates" becomes "Follow pull request templates". Settings search now matches "pr description", "pull request", "merge request", and "commit message". The user guide names the section. Setting keys, stored values, and the server prompt are unchanged.

title: feat(source-control): add Cursor Origin provider
author: maria-rcks
head: 4ee5b1f3525c4b6b716c3538ccfc3c6c7cfc6ea8
body:
## Problem

T3 Code can't work with repositories hosted on [Cursor Origin](https://cursor.com/docs/origin) (`origin.cursor.com`). Origin remotes show up as unknown hosts, so there's no pull request panel, publish target, or clone source for them.

## Change

Adds `packages/source-control-cursor-origin`, a source control driver registered next to GitCafe and GitHub. It signs in through the `origin` CLI. REST calls go over HTTPS with the session token from `origin auth token`, which is kept in memory for up to 5 minutes, so the server never writes an Origin token to disk.

- **Projects:** the driver recognizes `origin.cursor.com` remotes, clones over HTTPS from Add Project, and publishes local repos. Published repos come out private: Origin ignores visibility on create, so the driver patches the repo to private right after creating it.
- **Pull requests:** create, list (with Load more), detail, checks, mergeability, diff, comments, review threads, and reviews work. The panel can merge, squash, close, reopen, convert to draft, mark ready, edit, and check out a PR (`origin pr checkout N`). Origin has no rebase merge, so the menu doesn't offer it.
- **Stacks:** Origin merges a stacked PR together with every open PR below it, so Merge on a PR whose parent is still open is refused with a message pointing at the parent.
- **Links:** `cursor.com/codebase///pull/` resolves to the project's PR, and "Open on Cursor Origin" links back.
- **Viewed marks:** Origin has no API for viewed file [...]

threads.body:
🟡 **Medium** `server/OriginPullRequestProvider.ts:362`

For a PR whose `base.ref` is `refs/heads/main`, this requests `heads/refs/heads/main`, so the Git ref lookup fails and `mergeabilityOf` reports `unknown` instead of using the prepared merge's definite answer. Strip the `refs/heads/` prefix before adding `heads/`.

```suggestion
            path: `${OriginCli.originRepositoryPath(repository)}/git/ref/${encodeURIComponent(`heads/${branch.replace(/^refs\/heads\//u, "")}`)}`,
```

replies.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria

Not changing this. Origin returns `base.ref` as the bare branch name. The live API gives `"base":{"ref":"main"}`, and the panel shows `main ← feat/wave`. So the `heads/${branch}` path is correct.

threads.body:
🟠 **High** `server/OriginPullRequestProvider.ts:601`

Repositories with more than 100 matching pull requests cannot reach older results because this method always returns the first page and sets `continues` to `false`. It discards `page.nextPageToken` and never sends `input.cursor` as `pageToken`; propagate the token through `resumeAfter` and use the incoming cursor for the next request.

No longer relevant as of e8dd3e969fdd7d87d676b232b09feb146c92aa8b

replies.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria

Fixed in 707e7abeaf. Origin's page token is about 700 base64 characters, too long for the service cursor's `resumeAfter` (128 chars from `[\w.:~+-]`). The provider now keeps the token in an in-memory map and puts a hash key in `resumeAfter`. In the dev app, Load more on the Origin list grew it from 100 to 198 rows.

A push or retarget between `getPull` and this request makes `/pulls/N/files` return the newer version's patch, which this loader caches under the earlier `base...head` key for an hour. Callers requesting the earlier version then receive a mismatched diff; pin the files request to those commits or verify the PR version before caching the result.

No longer relevant as of e8dd3e969fdd7d87d676b232b09feb146c92aa8b

replies.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria

Fixed in 707e7abeaf. The `/files` read is now followed by a fresh read of the pull request, and the patch is cached for an hour only when that read still names the same `base...head`. Origin's `/files` ignores version parameters and `/compare` returns no files, so the patch can't be pinned in the request itself.

Single-line review threads with `endLine: 0` are returned with `line: null`, so `PullRequestCodeTab` renders their comments detached from the reviewed line. threads.body:
** Major** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Do not leave a published repository team-visible when the privacy update fails.**

`createRepository` runs in two steps. First, the POST creates the repository. Origin creates it as internal, which is visible to the whole team. Then, a separate PATCH sets `visibility: "private"`.

The PATCH can fail after the POST succeeds. Causes include a timeout, a 429, a 5xx, or a 401 after the retry. In that case the effect fails, but the repository stays internal. The user sees a generic publish error. A retry cannot recover, because the POST now fails with "already exists". The docs state that Origin repositories "are published privately", so this failure path breaks a documented privacy promise without telling the user.

Proposed fix:
- Retry the PATCH a bounded number of times.
- If the PATCH still fails, return a specific error. The error must say that the repository was created but is still visible to the team, and must name the repository so the user can fix it.

✅ Confirmed as addressed by @maria-rcks

replies.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria

Fixed in 707e7abeaf. The make-private PATCH retries twice. If it still fails, publish reports that `owner/name` was created but is still visible to the Cursor team, and asks the user to set it to private on cursor.com.

🟡 **Medium** `server/originPullRequests.ts:372`

Copied files with a different `previousFilename` are emitted with `rename from`/`rename to`, so the patch incorrectly says the source file was moved and no longer exists. Branch on `file.status === "copied"` and emit `copy from`/`copy to` headers instead.

```diff
-        ...(oldPath !== file.filename
-          ? [
-              `similarity index ${file.patch ? 0 : 100}%`,
-              `rename from ${quoteGitPatchPath(oldPath)}`,
-              `rename to ${quoteGitPatchPath(file.filename)}`,
-            ]
-          : []),
+        ...(oldPath !== file.filename
+          ? [
+              `similarity index ${file.patch ? 0 : 100}%`,
+              `${file.status === "copied" ? "copy" : "rename"} from ${quoteGitPatchPath(oldPath)}`,
+              `${file.status === "copied" ? "copy" : "rename"} to ${quoteGitPatchPath(file.filename)}`,
+            ]
+          : []),
```

title: feat(web): send messages while attachments upload
author: maria-rcks
head: ed08faf4bdada16051f4ebe8eaa096a3f8fe1aae
body:
![Image attached, sent at 0% upload, message shows at once, Haiku replies after the upload lands](https://uploads-production-47e4.up.railway.app/files/529d492a-a614-4454-93ca-2f39b93085fa/after.mp4)

![Message in the timeline and composer cleared while the upload is still in flight](https://uploads-production-47e4.up.railway.app/files/221ecd34-cf97-439b-9143-98ed45d207d7/during-upload.png)

![Haiku's reply after the upload finished and the thread started](https://uploads-production-47e4.up.railway.app/files/63a1edd9-9441-4696-8efc-3f0e7dacd6a7/complete.png)

Sending was disabled while an image or file attachment was still uploading ("Attachment still uploading"), so a big attachment meant waiting on a greyed-out send button.

Send now works mid-upload. The message appears right away, the composer clears, and the turn (or the new thread, for drafts) starts once the uploads land. If an upload fails, the message goes back into the composer with the failed attachment and its retry control, like any other failed send. Question answers and sends that would decline shown approvals still wait for uploads first, since those can't be undone. Mobile already allowed this.

Verified in the dev app with uploads slowed to 6s in the page: sent at 0%, the composer cleared, and Claude Haiku 5.5 answered about the image after the upload finished. Not exercised at runtime: a forced upload failure and navigating away mid-upload.

Written with `claude-opus-5-5` in Claude Code.

Reviewed with sol-l [...]

threads.body:
🟠 **High** `chat/useComposerSend.ts:989`

When a send has pending approvals and an attachment upload fails, `declinePendingApprovals` still declines the approvals before `prepareTurnAttachments` rejects, so no message is sent but the agent's approval decision is changed. Wait for the uploads to succeed and verify they are available before declining approvals.

replies.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria

Fixed in the latest commit. When the send would decline shown approvals, it now waits for the uploads and checks they're ready before declining. If one failed, it stops with "Retry or remove failed uploads before sending." and leaves the approvals alone.

threads.body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift**

**Keep a pending send recoverable across reloads.**

If a user reloads after the composer clears but before an upload finishes, the turn has not started and the draft is already empty. Upload jobs and the optimistic message do not provide a durable recovery path. Keep the pending send in persisted draft or outbox state until the turn starts, or restore it after a reload. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/08b4d3e61a4641612bc0b1aae6922eac3cc522e2/apps/web/src/composerDraftStore.ts))

replies.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria

Leaving this as is. The composer already clears before the turn is acknowledged today: worktree prep and `startThreadTurn` both run after the clear, and a reload during them drops the optimistic message the same way. This PR makes that window longer by the upload time but doesn't create it. A durable outbox would be a separate change.

threads.body:

author: juliusmarminge
head: 0727bded228e92fc3eb2bbca0831abddb2134d45
body:
## Problem

On iPhones with the floating glass tab bar, the compose button beside the workspace tabs can be drawn over a tab (usually Settings) instead of 16pt to the right of the bar. `WorkspaceTabBar.layoutSubviews` keeps only tab buttons whose converted size exactly equals their bounds size (the check from https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/28955 that skips the glass lens's magnified copy of the row). Converting a rect through the view hierarchy isn't exact in floating point, so at some bar widths real buttons fail the `==` comparison. The row then ends early and compose is placed after the wrong tab, or is never placed when no button passes.

Reproduced on current main in the real app (Expo dev client, iPhone 15 Pro simulator, 393pt, iOS 27.2, Chats selected). The stock bar width is correct on that runtime, so the bar width was stepped 1/3pt (one device pixel) at a time through the JS host inset. 16 of 28 widths placed compose wrongly: at a 13.6667pt inset compose covers Settings (the reported symptom), and at 12.3333pt it covers PRs/Usage.

## Change

The filter now compares converted and local sizes with a tolerance of less than 1pt on width and height instead of exact equality. That absorbs conversion rounding, while the lens copy (about 1.16×, so roughly 13pt wider and 9pt taller than a real tab button) is still excluded.

body:
## Problem

On web and desktop, opening a new side chat (the panel's "Side chat" entry, its `S` key, or the command palette) put keyboard focus on the side chat's **Bring back** button instead of its message input. Typing right after opening the side chat went nowhere.

Repro: open a thread with a finished reply, open the right panel, choose "Side chat", type `hi`. Expected: `hi` appears in the side chat's input. Actual: focus ring on Bring back, nothing typed.

## Change

Opening a panel surface already requests focus for the `panel` workspace area, and `focusArea` prefers a `[contenteditable="true"]` there. The side chat renders `ChatView` inside the panel, so its message input sits in a nested `composer` area. The preferred-target lookup required each match to belong directly to the panel area, so it skipped the input and fell back to the first button in the surface, Bring back.

When focus is requested for the panel, the preferred lookup now accepts matches in nested areas. F6 navigation keeps the old rule, because it visits the side chat's own areas separately. Without that, a maximized side chat would send F6 from its input straight back to the same input. Restoring the last focused control and the plain-button fallback still only consider the panel's own controls. Only the side chat nests areas inside the panel, so other surfaces are unaffected.

title: perf(server): macOS worktrees open 2x faster by cloning a cached checkout
author: t3dotgg
head: 7685d23a73c6d8c93af1d09fc7b26c6b64292695
body:
New worktree threads are slow on Mac. On T3 Code's own repo (31,741 files), `git worktree add` takes about 1.6 s because it writes every file, and the first `git status` in the new worktree takes another 1–1.6 s because its index is racy and Git re-reads everything.

Now, as an opt-in Labs beta, T3 keeps a few recent checkouts of each repo in the T3 home `caches` folder and clones new worktrees from them with APFS copy-on-write. Creating a worktree is about twice as fast, and the first status is about 6× faster. Any case the cache can't reproduce exactly uses `git worktree add`, as before.

| M4 Pro, 31,741 files, median of 5 | createWorktree | First `git status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock `git worktree add` | 1,592 ms | 1,035–1,636 ms |
| Cache at the same commit | 893 ms | 201 ms |
| Cache 10–50 commits older | ~1,060 ms | ~230 ms |

## How it works

- After a worktree is created, a background build caches its tree: Git writes it into a private folder, and T3 records the files' stat data in a copy of the index.
- To create a worktree, T3 registers it with `git worktree add --no-checkout` and clones the cached files with macOS `clonefile(2)`, through `ffi-rs`, which the server already ships. Then it rewrites the index stat data so Git trusts the clones without reading them. If the cache is at an older commit, `read-tree -m -u` writes only the changed files. The post-checkout hook still runs.

title: fix(mobile): SVG markers with orient="auto-start-reverse" no longer crash Android
author: juliusmarminge
head: 47fe786e1524be8e0c12cab7860e1424b1dd3618
body:
## Problem

The Android app crashes when a chat shows an inline SVG image with a marker whose `orient="auto-start-reverse"`, and it crashes again every time that thread is reopened. react-native-svg's Android `MarkerView.renderMarker` calls `Double.parseDouble` on every orient value except `"auto"`, so the keyword throws an uncaught `NumberFormatException` on the main thread. Upstream 15.16.1 has the same line.

Reproduced on main (71c2d3a302) with the reporter's SVG on a Pixel 9 emulator (API 36): a real agent turn saved the file into the workspace and replied with `![Marker repro](/abs/path/marker-repro.svg)`. Opening that thread in the Android dev client closed the app to the launcher. Reopening it after a relaunch did the same. The same SVG with `orient="auto"` rendered.

## Change

A pnpm patch of `react-native-svg@15.16.0` (Android only), plus its `patchedDependencies` entry and override pin. In `MarkerView.renderMarker`:

- `auto` keeps the path angle.
- `auto-start-reverse` adds 180° to the start marker only, as SVG 2 defines it.
- Any other value is parsed as a number. A null or unparsable value (`bogus`, `""`, `90deg`) falls back to 0° instead of throwing.

Other effects:

- `orient="-1"` used to collide with the old internal `-1` meaning "auto", so it followed the path tangent. It now rotates by −1°, as written (R5).
- Angles with units (`90deg`) are not supported; they now draw at 0° instead of crashing.
- iOS does not crash on this SVG and is unchanged.
- This is [...]

title: feat(mobile): iOS socket compresses traffic
author: juliusmarminge
head: ab4a66b3a3ce5de092d5f767a2fbcc12dcb0a879
body:
React Native's iOS WebSocket is SocketRocket, which never negotiates permessage-deflate. The server offers compression (`perMessageDeflate: true`), but every frame to an iPhone still arrives uncompressed. Android already compresses: OkHttp sends the extension on every handshake.

## Fix

- A local Expo module, `apps/mobile/modules/t3-web-socket`, dials through `URLSessionWebSocketTask`, which offers permessage-deflate on every handshake.
- A small `WebSocketLike` wrapper gives Effect's socket layer what it needs on iOS:
  - each socket reports its end once, with the server's close code and reason
  - writes after close are dropped, as browsers do
  - disposing the layer finalizes open sockets
- Dev clients built without the module keep using the global WebSocket.
- Android is unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Maintainer-authored. It fixes the triaged bug https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/21183 and replaces https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/24931 at the maintainers' direction. Layer 2 of 2, on https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/32287.

title: perf(mobile): thread list resumes from the saved cache, and large gaps reload over gzip HTTP
author: juliusmarminge
head: 460a65be963cf7a0d9b400c7cc15b7fc77e55aed
body:
On a cold start every client downloaded the full thread list, even when its saved copy was a few events behind. When a client did resume from a cursor beyond the server's replay cap (1,000 events, 8 MB), the server answered with a full snapshot over the socket. iOS does not compress that, so it arrived at 1.37 MB instead of the 88 KB the gzip HTTP route costs.

## Fix

- **Resume from the saved cache.** The shell cache now records the snapshot its rows came from as `origin`: server version, database migration, omission flags, and `snapshotAt`. A client whose cache matches its subscription and is under 12 hours old subscribes with `afterSequence` instead of loading a fresh snapshot. Replay never renews `snapshotAt`, so drift stays bounded.
- **`snapshot-required`.** A resuming client sends `httpSnapshotFallback: true`. If the server cannot replay that cursor (over the gap cap or pruned), it answers with one `snapshot-required` item and doesn't send the snapshot. The client then loads the gzip HTTP snapshot and subscribes again from it.
  - A cursor from a snapshot that was just loaded never sends the flag, so a refusal cannot loop.
  - Old servers ignore the flag, and old clients never send it.
- Items buffered from a superseded session are dropped, and a resume that catches up bumps `generation`.

title: perf(mobile): sign DPoP proofs natively, up to 355x faster on Android
author: camchis
head: 734c43c79fd94e7d70986bfa5f3c059ea1b875b7
body:
## Problem

Mobile signs every T3 Connect DPoP proof with `@noble/curves`, because Hermes has no SubtleCrypto. Hermes interprets noble's BigInt code, which is slow:

- **Cold key load, once per app session.** Before any relay request, `ManagedRelay.authorize` loads the signer's thumbprint. That calls `p256.getPublicKey` to check the stored key, the first base-point multiply in the process, so noble builds its 8-bit window table on the JS thread. On a Solana Seeker this took **924 ms** (923–925 ms across 5 launches), the whole time with the JS thread blocked.
- **Every proof after that.** `p256.sign` took **7.1 ms** on the JS thread, so a full `createProof` took 7.7 ms. Each relay request and DPoP-authorized environment HTTP request pays it.

## Fix

Key generation, the stored-key check, and signing move to three `AsyncFunction`s on the existing `T3NativeControls` module:

- **iOS:** CryptoKit `P256.Signing`. `signature(for:)` hashes with SHA-256 and returns the raw `r‖s` pair JWS uses.
- **Android:** the platform `SHA256withECDSA` (Conscrypt). Its DER output is converted to `r‖s`. JCA cannot derive a public point from a scalar, so the stored-key check signs and verifies a probe.

Everything else stays the same:

- Keys stay in Expo SecureStore in the same private-JWK format. Existing installs keep their key, so relay sessions bound to its thumbprint keep working.
- `@noble/curves` is no longer a mobile dependency.
- Web keeps its non-extractable WebCrypto key. The server and  [...]

## Problem

The Secrets page says `op` must be signed in on the machine running the T3 Code server. On a remote or headless server, a desktop 1Password sign-in asks for approval on that machine, where the remote user can't answer it, so the secret can't be read. Nothing tells users what to do instead.

## Change

Two short how-tos under `docs/user/`, linked from `secrets.md` and `docs/README.md`:

- `secrets-1password-service-account.md`: set up a service account and `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`.
- `secrets-1password-connect.md`: use an existing Connect server with `OP_CONNECT_HOST` and `OP_CONNECT_TOKEN`.

Docs only, no code changes.

A small docs gap, raised in a maintainer discussion about running secret providers on remote environments. No code, contract, or UI change.

## Problem

When a provider instance had a stored sensitive environment variable, adding a second row with the same name and committing it deleted the stored secret. This happened whether the second row was empty and sensitive, or not sensitive. The first row kept showing "Stored secret", so removing the duplicate left a variable that claimed a value it no longer had. The secret could not be recovered.

title: fix(web): rich text previews keep paragraphs that end with a backslash
author: geezoria
head: a7dcda0017ab3f6c49732ca21097f7f3443d2604
body:
## Problem

The rich text (`.rtf`) file preview runs every paragraph of a document saved by macOS TextEdit into one line.

The RTF spec treats a backslash followed by a carriage return or line feed as `\par`. TextEdit ends every paragraph this way, not with an explicit `\par`:

```rtf
\f0\fs24 \cf0 First\
Second\
\
Third}
```

`openRtf` handled the pair as an unknown control symbol and skipped it, so the preview showed `FirstSecondThird`. An explicit `\par` in the same position already renders as a line break.

## Change

In `openRtf`'s control-symbol branch, a backslash before `\n` or `\r` now adds the same `` that `\par` adds, and respects hidden destinations in the same way. For `\`, the `\r` is consumed with the backslash, and the loop already ignores the bare `\n` that follows, so CRLF files give one break, not two.

## Scope and approval

This is a very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so it uses CONTRIBUTING's exception for those. It is a one-line parsing correction for a form the RTF spec defines and the most common macOS editor writes. It changes nothing for documents that use `\par`.

body:
## Problem

In the Cmd/Ctrl+P file picker and the Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F content search, the Escape that cancels or leaves an IME composition in Safari sends the overlay back to the command palette. A key that belongs to an IME composition should stay in the input.

## Change

It skipped keys flagged by `isComposing`, but not `keyCode === 229`. The handler consumed it and dispatched `BackToCommand`. It now skips `keyCode === 229` too. That is the guard the palette's own input already uses for Enter and Tab (`CommandPalette.tsx`).

The handler runs on `window` in the capture phase, ahead of Base UI's dialog dismiss. With the handler skipping the key, that dismiss decides next, and it already ignores an Escape that follows `compositionend`, so in Safari the overlay stays put.

author: spoukyii
head: 07c7b1798cad28edde6a7c7627fa614c2af13e5b
body:
## Problem

Deleting the thread you are viewing opens the newest other thread in its project, but the pick includes side chats and running subagents, which have no sidebar row of their own. So the app can open a side chat or subagent on its own, or, when the pick is a side chat of the deleted thread, open an empty new draft even though other threads are listed.

Expected: the fallback skips side chats and subagents, as it already skips snoozed and settled threads.

## Change

`getFallbackThreadIdAfterDelete` picks from every thread shell the environment streams. It now also skips threads for which `isSidebarHiddenThread` is true, beside the snoozed and settled checks #29643 added. title: perf(web): long reasoning previews format in linear time (600 ms → 1.3 ms median)
author: Yuruzuu
head: 29379d12da92bf442dd5cffd7cdd80a6874709c4
body:
## Problem

Long reasoning makes the chat timeline do a lot of main-thread work. The long thought preview and the expanded active reasoning header both run `remarkThoughtPreview`. On the largest reasoning entry in a real local database (150 KB), that one plugin took about 600 ms on every format. Parsing the same entry takes about 39 ms. While reasoning streams, the active header reformats the whole accumulated text on each accepted update, so the cost adds up.

## Change

`remarkThoughtPreview` (`apps/web/src/components/chat/TimelineWorkEntryRow.logic.ts`) flattens Markdown into text nodes. Each time it appended an AST fragment, it concatenated the fragment onto the current text node and ran `replace(/\s+/g, " ")` over the whole accumulated string again. With one long text run, the cost was quadratic in reasoning length.

The plugin now collects the fragments of each text run and normalizes the joined run once. A run ends before a math node and at the end of the tree. Collapsing every whitespace run to one space gives the same result whether you do it per fragment or once on the joined text, so the output tree is unchanged: same nodes, same empty text nodes between math, same trimming and fallback.

Surfaces: web and desktop (desktop wraps web). Mobile renders reasoning through its own native Markdown path and does not use this plugin. No contract, server or provider changes.

title: fix(web): deleting a thread clears its side chats' drafts
author: saphid
head: f938455a3eff6b43bfce52ce09d824bf59fd65cd
body:
## Problem

When you delete a thread, the server also deletes its side chats. The web client clears the deleted thread's composer draft and releases its staged uploads, but it does not do this for the side chats. Deleting a side chat with its own Delete button also leaves its draft behind.

So any text or attachments typed into a side chat's composer stay in the persisted draft store, and its staged uploads are never released. Side chat ids are never reused, so nothing in the UI can reach or clean up these drafts.

## Change

- `useThreadActions.deleteThread`: after a successful delete, release uploads and clear the draft for each side chat of the deleted thread too. Side chats are found by `lineage.sideChat` and `lineage.parentThreadId`, the same way client-runtime groups them by parent.
- Archived threads that aren't loaded on this client: maria-rcks added a `threadFamily` read so their side chats are found too. If that read fails, the delete falls back to the thread shells this client holds and still runs, because a cleanup lookup must never block deletion.
- `SideChatPane` Delete: after a successful delete, release the side chat's uploads and clear its draft, as `deleteThread` already does for a thread.

## Scope and approval

Very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so no prior issue: deleting a thread already clears its own draft and uploads, and this applies the same cleanup to the side chats deleted with it.

Prior PRs: [#28559](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/ [...]

author: thatsnoi
head: baf3e88dd500e76e91829da71dd65cfa692503a5
body:
## Problem

The preview annotation tool can't annotate inside a page's dialog or popover. The overlay lives in a closed shadow root under ``, so a page's `document` listeners see its pointer and focus events retargeted to the overlay host, which is outside any open dialog. With Radix UI (and other libraries that listen the same way):

- **Popover / DropdownMenu (non-modal):** picking an element inside it closes it as soon as the comment field takes focus (`onFocusOutside`). The picked element leaves the DOM.
- **Modal Dialog / AlertDialog:** the focus trap (`focusout` with a `relatedTarget` outside the dialog) pulls focus back into the dialog, so the comment can't be typed. Any click on the overlay toolbar is an outside `pointerdown` and closes the dialog. The attached element then reports a zero rect and a generic selector.
- **react-remove-scroll** (Radix modals) cancels wheel events over the overlay's editor and style panel.

The overlay already isolates `keydown`; this fixes the pointer, focus and wheel/touch side.

## Why this is a small fix for an obvious bug

Annotating an element inside an open dialog or popover is a normal use of the tool, and today it either closes the dialog or makes the comment field unusable. The fix is confined to the overlay's own event wiring in `PickPreload.ts`, is active only during an annotation session, and is removed in `teardown`. No contract, UI or default changes.

title: perf(web): Appearance settings no longer re-probe fonts on every open
author: chelokot
head: 12c4137386bfeb3ec7ead59f1ac56d58f60791b6
body:
## Problem

Opening Settings → Appearance blocked the main thread for over 100 ms on every visit, while other settings pages open in about 15 ms. Each font row resolved the default font labels ("Inter Variable", "Liberation Mono") in its own `useState` initializer. Each resolution appends probe spans to `body` and reads their width, which forces a layout of the whole document, including the thread behind the dialog. That added up to 24 forced layouts per open.

## Change

The default labels depend only on the installed fonts, so `TypographySettings` now resolves them once per session, after `document.fonts` has loaded, and every row and every later open reuses them. Before the web fonts load, each mount resolves them again as it did before, so a fallback label is never cached. The installed-font list in `appearanceFonts.ts` is cached the same way, so a font installed mid-session shows up as the default after a reload, as it already does in the picker.

Web and desktop share this code. Mobile has its own settings UI and isn't touched. No contract or server changes.

## Scope and approval

This fits the small, focused exception in CONTRIBUTING.md: one file and 13 lines that remove repeated forced layouts, with no change to behavior, rendering, or contracts.

## Verification

Desktop nightly `0.1.7-nightly.20261101.4048` on Linux with a copy of real data: 124 threads, with a thread open behind the dialog. I compared the shipped app with the same app after applying this memoizati [...]

head: d975ea11e7e879f29b8057b5d1f8aa08fc13f28a
body:
## Problem

If you archive a thread that has unsent composer text, a staged attachment, or an opened terminal drawer, then delete it from Settings → Archived threads, that state is never cleaned up. The composer draft and terminal UI state stay in local storage for a thread that no longer exists, and the staged uploads are never released, so their pending uploads also stay on the server.

The archived branch now calls `releaseComposerDraftUploads`, `clearComposerDraftForThread` and `clearTerminalUiState` with the thread ref after a successful delete. `clearProjectDraftThreadById` is left out. It needs the thread's project id, which is not available without a shell, and it only maps project draft threads, which are never archived server threads.

A page redirect during loading reaches its target but shows a `navigate.loadURL` error. The temporary listener is removed when the operation ends.

### Verified in a real dev environment

verified on linux at `015a6eb5ccb44d52bd67be3c23aedc475c39a955`. installed and ran separate main and pr worktrees, one dev stack at a time. created a real git project and thread through the web app, then ran real Codex `gpt-6.1-sol` turns through the local provider proxy. used repo Playwright with Chrome for the web flow and Electron 44.10.0's actual Browser panel for native navigation.

main reproduced the original error on an immediate page redirect. the original pr removed that error but silently swallowed an unsaved page's blocked navigation. the scoped fix observes `will-prevent-unload` so blocked navigation still reports failure while redirects and same-url superseded loads succeed.

final runtime checks passed: redirect without a toast; unsaved draft blocks navigation, retains its text and reports the error; saving permits navigation; refused connections retain their error; reload during loading reaches the same address without a toast. the existing regression wa [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Preserve errors for blocked navigations.**

If the current page prevents unloading, Electron also rejects `loadURL` with `ERR_ABORTED`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.10.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc)) This catch reports success even though the requested page did not load, and the `did-fail-load` handler also ignores the error.

Distinguish a superseding navigation from a blocked unload. Propagate the blocked-unload error and add a regression case.

✅ Addressed in commit f1d4bff

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Handle superseding navigations to the same URL.**

If a page reloads itself before a slow resource finishes, Electron rejects the original `loadURL` with `ERR_ABORTED` and the same URL. This condition propagates the error, so the user still sees a navigation error even though the reload proceeds. Electron does not require the replacement URL to differ. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.10.0/lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts))

Track the second main-frame navigation instead of comparing URLs. Keep blocked-unload errors reportable.

✅ Addressed in commit 015a6eb

## Problem

While an agent edits files, each working tree change re-renders the whole chat view, and the side chat too when one is open. The chat view never shows those file counts.

title: fix(mobile): nested code blocks no longer overlap the next message on Android
author: juliusmarminge
head: 0a46b50f4d4d3839d19736d902281379122f66bb
body:
## Problem

On Android, an assistant reply with fenced code blocks inside list items is laid out shorter than it is drawn. The copy/fork/time row lands on the reply's last lines, and the closing paragraphs run under the next message. Reopening the thread does not help. Main still does this: upstream [#1102](https://github.com/software-mansion/enriched-markdown/pull/1102), already in main's `t3.18-4287c5d3` archive, fixes one span pair, but main's Android client still overlaps (capture below).

## Change

This vendors a fixed `react-native-enriched-markdown` archive and changes nothing else.

The Android text view lays its text out through an insertion-ordered span wrapper (`InsertionOrderedSpannable`). Measurement built its `StaticLayout`s from the renderer's bare `SpannableStringBuilder`, which the framework reads in a different span order. When two `LineHeightSpan`s share a line, as a list's line height and a nested code block's margin spacer do, measurement and drawing can disagree about that line's height. The fork commit adds `inViewSpanOrder()` next to the wrapper. `SegmentHeightMeasurer.createStaticLayout` and `MeasurementStore.buildMeasureLayout` build their layouts through it, so measurement reads spans the way the view draws them. Drawn spacing is unchanged.

title: fix(server): delegated Claude tasks report the model that ran
author: shivamhwp
head: 1a75f4c27b41e3a3ec88a8e7112d1fae9c5698f8
body:
## Problem
When Claude runs a different model than a delegated task asked for, the parent only sees the requested one. For example, an organization that only allows Sonnet makes an Opus request run on Sonnet. `task_status`, the thread's runs and the completion message all name Opus, so the parent reports an "Opus review" that Sonnet did. Closes https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/27705.

## Change
- The Claude adapter now saves, on each provider turn, the model Claude reports on the root agent's assistant messages. Native subagents and CLI notices are skipped. The name is normalized through the model catalog, dropping a trailing `-YYYYMMDD` date when the catalog doesn't list the dated ID, so `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` counts as `claude-opus-4-5`.
- `task_status` and thread `recentRuns` gain `executedModel`, which is null when unavailable. `task_status` takes it from the run that produced the result.
- When the model that ran differs from the one requested, the delegated result starts with "Requested model X; the provider reported running Y." Tasks in a linked environment get the same note, taken from the remote thread's run. Older linked environments omit the field, so it reads as unknown.

## Evidence
A real Claude Haiku 5.5 parent in the web client delegates a review to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, then prints its `task_status`. Neither the account nor any cheap route made Claude really substitute a model: retired models are refused with an error, not swapped. So the child's [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Use the stored result transfer’s source run for completed tasks.**

For legacy child tasks, `taskResultRun` uses `progress.resultRun`, which selects the latest terminal work run. A later child run can change `model` and `executedModel` while `derivedResult` still returns the stored `task.result`. The result transfer records the producing run in `sourcePoint.runId`. Use that run when the result is stored. Keep the latest-run behavior for unstored results.

The pre-change code used `childRun?.modelSelection`, so this model-selection mismatch was introduced by selecting `taskResultRun`. `executedModel` is new in this change.

✅ Addressed in commit 3aacf80

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Limit provider notices to the active attempt's provider turns.**

`rootProviderNotices` selects root notices by `runId` and `rootNodeId`. It does not check which attempt produced them. A run can have several attempts, so a root notice from an earlier attempt can pass the filter. `subagentResultForRun` then pairs that notice with the model from the active attempt. The delegated result can then show a provider notice that belongs to a different attempt. Each provider turn records its `runAttemptId`, and each system notice records its `providerTurnId`. Select notices whose `providerTurnId` belongs to a provider turn of `run.activeAttemptId`. An attempt can contain several provider turns, so match every turn of that attempt. Notices without a `providerTurnId` cannot be attributed to an attempt, so they are excluded.

✅ Addressed in commit 3aacf80

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Compare equivalent model identifiers before reporting a substitution.**

The Claude adapter converts a reported alias to a catalog slug, but this comparison leaves `requestedModel` unchanged. If a selection uses an alias for the model Claude reports, the result incorrectly says Claude substituted the model. Normalize the requested Claude model for the comparison, while preserving its original value in the displayed note.

✅ Addressed in commits b229bfc to bd5c9d9

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Select the latest provider turn that reports a model.**

If a later turn in the active attempt completes without a model frame, `latestProviderTurnForAttempt` selects that turn and `executedModel` becomes undefined. An earlier turn in the same attempt can have the model that ran, but the delegated result then omits the substitution note. Select the highest-ordinal turn **with** a recorded model for this attribution.

## Problem

Asked to run a command that needs a sudo password (`run sudo dnf update for me`), agents in T3 Code stopped, said they could not type a password, and told the user to run it themselves or add a NOPASSWD sudoers rule. They never called `request_secret`, which already delivers a secret to a shell command through a private file. Every provider gets the shared T3 instruction, and its secret bullet never linked a password prompt from a requested command to `request_secret`; Claude cannot see the tool's own description because it sits behind ToolSearch. title: fix(mobile): Android navigation bar follows the app theme
author: vinceglb
head: 1f02fac4683c8d33c1d3492afb21d79f142d3e2d
body:
## Problem

On Android, the navigation bar's light/dark style ignores the app theme. React Native sets it once, at launch, from the system theme (`WindowUtil.enableEdgeToEdge()`), and nothing updates it afterwards. `MainActivity` handles `uiMode` changes itself, so it is not recreated either.

When the app theme differs from the system theme, Android draws the wrong contrast scrim behind a tappable navigation bar. That happens when Settings > Appearance is set to Light or Dark, and when the system theme changes while the app is running. On a Galaxy Z Fold unfolded with gesture navigation, the result is a full-width light band under the gesture handle in a dark app, or a dark band in a light app. 3-button navigation shows the same thing.

To reproduce: Galaxy Z Fold, unfolded, gesture navigation, system theme light, then Settings > Appearance > Dark.

## Change

- `T3NativeControls` gets `setNavigationBarStyle(light)`. It sets `isAppearanceLightNavigationBars` on the current window, on the main thread.
  - Below Android 10 it does nothing, because React Native paints the bar color itself there.
- `AppContent` calls it from an effect on `themeAppearance`, next to the existing `` that already does this for the status bar.
- iOS is unchanged.

I first tried re-applying the style natively on configuration changes. The bar then flipped about 0.5 s before React repainted the content. Driving it from `themeAppearance` keeps the bar in step with the content.

## Scope and approval

No [...]

The React Native 0.88 default remains based on the system theme, so navigation-bar icons can use the wrong appearance. Change the guard in `T3NativeControlsModule.kt` to the API 26 boundary.

title: fix(desktop): recording cursor stays above modal dialogs and popovers
author: mateusjunges
head: e1244205e77338fee1a9d347ec8a716f5ad693f2
body:
## Problem

When a desktop preview tab is being recorded and the page opens a native modal (`` opened with `showModal()`, as Laravel Flux modals do), the recording cursor disappears for as long as the modal is open. `installRecordingCursor` draws the human arrow and the agent pointer as `position:fixed` divs with `z-index:2147483647` appended to ``, but elements in the browser's top layer (modal dialogs, popovers, fullscreen elements) always paint above normal content regardless of z-index. The modal's `::backdrop` covers the whole viewport, so the cursor is hidden or tinted everywhere, not just behind the dialog box. Server browser recordings draw the cursor onto the encoded canvas and are not affected.

## Change

Both cursor elements are now `popover="manual"` and are shown as popovers right after they are appended, which puts them in the top layer. The top layer is ordered by insertion, so whenever the page adds something to it the cursors are hidden and shown again to move them back to the front. A `MutationObserver` on the `open` attribute catches `show()` and `showModal()`, a capturing `toggle` listener catches page popovers opening (ignoring our own elements and closing transitions), and `fullscreenchange` covers fullscreen.
