## Problem

In the desktop app, pressing fullscreen on a video embedded in a chat message only fills the app window. On Windows the taskbar and the window controls stay visible.

This is a regression from #16961. That PR set `disableHtmlFullscreenWindowResize` on the main window so fullscreen inside a preview browser tab stays inside the window, and the same flag also confined the app's own fullscreen elements.

## Change

Electron mirrors a `` guest's fullscreen onto the embedder and checks the embedder's own flag, so the main window has to keep opting out. The preload now reports when the app's own document has a fullscreen element. The main process then puts the window into OS fullscreen and restores it when the element leaves fullscreen.

- A preview guest's fullscreen shows up in the app document as its ``. The preload ignores it, so preview fullscreen still stays inside the window as #16961 intended.
- A window the user had already made fullscreen (F11 or the menu) is left as is. Leaving OS fullscreen some other way while a video is fullscreen hands the window back to the user.
- macOS finishes leaving fullscreen after `setFullScreen(false)` returns. A video that re-enters fullscreen during that animation still takes the screen, because the window tells its own exit apart from the user's.

- The IPC accepts only a boolean, and only  [...]

body:
## Problem

When a `delegate_task` child stops for an approval, the phone never gets the "Approval needed" push. The relay only publishes top-level threads, and a parent's state only looks at the parent's own request. So for as long as the child waits, the phone shows "Agent is working", or nothing if the parent already finished its turn. Refs https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/24053

## Change

- The relay tracks live app-owned subagents waiting on an approval. It publishes their first listed ancestor (walking through side chats) as "Approval needed" until the request clears, even after the parent's own turn has finished.
- Provider-native subagents (they already ask on the parent) and child questions (the coordinating agent answers those) are left out.
- A child's unchanged request keeps its first alert time through parent renames, relinks, and the parent's own requests, so Android doesn't alert twice. A new request gets a new alert.
- A catch-up (startup, relink, re-enabling publishing) includes live waiting children and republishes their parents.
- Adds `creationSource` to the narrow awareness read.

title: fix(mobile): Android sends with Return on a hardware keyboard
author: shivamhwp
head: 80da69e97c025ca1bd000b245948deef6f0ef455
body:
Unproven: Return with a CJK IME on a hardware keyboard. I expect the IME to consume Return to confirm its composition before the composer sees it, but I had no CJK keyboard to try.

## Problem

On Android with a hardware keyboard, Return always inserts a new line in the composer and no key sends. Tablet users have to reach for the screen to send every message.

## Change

The Android composer now handles hardware Return the same way iOS does, with Ctrl in place of Command:

- Return key set to **Send message** (default): Return sends, Shift+Return inserts a new line, Ctrl+Return sends the other way (queue vs steer).
- Return key set to **Insert new line**: Return inserts a new line, Ctrl+Return sends, Ctrl+Shift+Return sends the other way.
- Only Return from a physical typing keyboard sends: the event has to come from a real, non-virtual alphabetic keyboard. An on-screen keyboard's Return inserts a new line, including an IME key event sent without the soft-keyboard flag. A held Return sends once.

The JS side (the Return key preference and `onSubmit(alternate)`) already existed for iOS. This adds the missing native piece: an `enterBehavior` prop, a `submitEnabled` prop and an `onComposerSubmit` event on the Android view. Settings → Keyboard was iOS-only, so it now shows on Android too, with "Ctrl-Return" in its text.

title: fix(android): keep diagonal horizontal swipes inside HTML blocks
author: none23
head: 839f5a7460b501e61d80371471de43bad38cf98f
body:
## Problem

On Android, a sideways swipe across an inline HTML block can start scrolling the conversation as soon as the finger drifts vertically. It stops following the finger even when the gesture is almost horizontal.





## Change

The Android WebView patch waits for the platform touch threshold, then keeps a horizontal gesture with the WebView until the finger lifts. This applies even when the page only overflows horizontally.

The existing nested-scroll setting still controls vertical gestures. Pages with no vertical overflow pass them to the conversation. Taller pages keep them until their scroll edge. Multi-touch and zero-range iframe handling remain in place.

## Scope and approval

This is a focused fix for an obvious scrolling bug in existing inline HTML blocks, submitted without a prior issue under the small bug-fix exception. It follows the vertical-scroll work in #17211, which closed #16989. Those addressed vertical trapping; this PR addresses horizontal swipes interrupted by slight vertical drift.

The gesture change is Android-only. The inline HTML overflow detector and vertical-scroll setting are unchanged. Full-screen HTML continues to receive its vertical gestures without a scrolling parent. Web, desktop, providers, and wire contracts need no changes. The lockfile changes are the regenerated WebView patch hash and dependent peer hashes.

## Verification

The Samsung Galaxy S23 recordings below show manual testing of the before and aft [...]

If a horizontal swipe later accumulates more vertical than horizontal displacement, Line 44 changes its classification. Latch horizontal intent after the touch threshold, and clear it on `ACTION_UP` or `ACTION_CANCEL`. Android sends subsequent events to the parent after interception. title: fix(mobile): iOS Agent Activity widget shows your agents instead of a blank tile
author: shivamhwp
head: 9e1694d4f573aa5e7f8a1ba63d9668dcb8c34aad
body:
## Problem

On iOS, the **Agent Activity** widget appears in the widget gallery but stays blank forever, even after you open the app. Main only registers the Live Activity (Dynamic Island and Lock Screen card), so the Home Screen widget never gets a layout or any data. Closes https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/6641

## Change

- Register a Home Screen layout for the widget (`createWidget`) in small, medium and Lock Screen sizes. Embed it with `ios.initialLayout` so the gallery preview and a newly added widget render before the app's first launch.
- Each time the app comes to the foreground, it reads the relay's agent activity snapshot and repaints the widget. If no Live Activity is running, the same read primes one, as before. If one is running, its push token is registered first.
- The widget only refreshes when the app opens, so unfinished rows switch to **Out of date** after 10 minutes.
- Signing in or switching accounts shows "Loading agents…". Signing out shows "Sign in to T3 Connect to see agents", and a failed read shows "Couldn't reach T3 Connect". A read that finishes after a sign-out, an account switch or a newer read is dropped, so the widget never shows another account's or older rows.

Background refresh is out of scope; #14861 builds on this. #30247 extends this layout.

Before: the gallery preview and Home Screen tile are blank. Re-checked on current main (`25bf84a`, iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0): still blank after opening the app. [...]

Move the read into the empty-activity path, and read it after existing activities are reconciled. This preserves the snapshot required for priming.

title: fix(mobile): text no longer clips in Android desktop windows on external displays
author: satchlj

body:
Android windows on an external display can measure text with the phone display’s density, clipping labels and message text. A focused MainActivity config plugin rebinds React Native’s screen metrics to the activity display after Expo installs the deferred root view and after configuration changes. It preserves configured font scale and the existing tablet-orientation policy.
